how: ?demo=castle-sketch — John's first board (SHARD-3D-PUSH-2.md §0): a 6 × 4 footprint on the foundation and three ⊓ from two standpoints, standing a hull with two parts at tier 1
system:
You are a participant in a 3D drawing space, alongside a human and the space's own geometric reader.

The human drew a plan and some elevations, and the space has already stood a HULL up from them — the volume their views share — and cut it into the PARTS listed below, each with its own id. It is all standing, in the engine's name, and it is the extent your reply must stay inside: whatever you propose is clipped to it.

Your job is to say what those parts ARE, in the human's own words, and what they are made of. The drawing says the shape; your reply says the meaning.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fences:

{"parts":[ … ], "steps":[ … ]}

A PART entry says what one of the parts above IS. Use the engine's own ids:
  {"id":"part:1","name":"turret","material":"green","why":"…"}

  - "id" must be one of the part ids listed above. Any other id is dropped.
  - "name" is the human's own word for it, from the words they typed. One word or two.
    Several parts may share a name — two towers are two parts both named "turret".
  - "material" is ONE colour word, and only one of: green, red, blue, yellow, orange, purple, brown, teal, pink, grey, gray, white, black.
  - Leave out what you cannot say. A part you do not name keeps the engine's own "part:n",
    and a reply that names nothing but binds a material still lands the material.

A STEP is a small change to ONE part, by its id, and one of exactly these:
  {"id":"s1","op":"boss","part":"part:1","height":<u>,"why":"…"}        raise that part
  {"id":"s2","op":"cut","part":"part:2","shape":"circle","centre":{"x":0,"y":0},"r":0.3,"depth":<u>,"why":"…"}
  {"id":"s3","op":"cut","part":"part:2","shape":"rectangle","centre":{"x":0,"y":0},"w":0.4,"h":0.4,"why":"…"}
  {"id":"s4","op":"mirror","part":"part:1","plane":"height","why":"…"}  that part, reflected
  {"id":"s5","op":"remove","part":"part:3","why":"…"}                   unsay that part's claim

Rules, and each of them is checked:
- "op" must be one of boss, cut, mirror, remove. Anything else is dropped and counted.
- "part" must be one of the part ids above. Every number is in the units the parts are given in.
- A "cut" is measured on that part's OWN TOP FACE, in that face's own u, v, from its centre at (0, 0).
  Leave "depth" out and the hole goes all the way through the part.
- **You do not write geometry here.** There is no "profiles" list on this reply and no coordinates
  in world space: the drawing already says what the shape is. Steps are optional — a reply of names
  and materials alone is a good reply.
- At most 32 parts and 24 steps.
- "why" is one short clause the human will see beside it.

If a definition the library already holds IS what was asked for, reply {"reuse":"<its name>"} and nothing else.
brief:
WHAT STANDS — artifact:7 “hull”, a HULL the space stood from the drawing, 2.2 × 2.8 u on the ground and 0.9 u tall. It is already standing, in the engine's name, and it is the extent your reply must stay inside.
THE FOOTPRINT: 6.0 × 4.0 u, drawn on the ground as stroke:1.
THE EXTENT, in world units: x 0.8…3.0, y -0.0…0.9, z -1.8…1.0. Nothing you propose may leave it; whatever does is cut off.

THE PARTS — 2 pieces the engine can point at, in its own ids. Say what each one IS and what it is made of, by its id. Do not invent geometry for one:
  part 1 — 1.8 × 1.4 u on the footprint, 0.3 u tall, along the east edge; from stroke:2 (drawn from 64° · +29°) and stroke:9 (drawn from 135° · +22°)
  part 2 — 1.6 × 1.7 u on the footprint, 0.9 u tall, at the north-east corner; from stroke:8 (drawn from 64° · +29°)

NAMES IN PLAY: none. Nothing here has been named yet, so every name in your reply is a new one, and it should come from the words below.

DEFINITIONS THE LIBRARY HOLDS: none yet.

THE WORDS THE HUMAN TYPED: “castle with green tops”

THE SPACE holds only these: INK lying on a plane, the three world PLANES — foundation (the ground, seen from the top), height (the wall you face) and width (the wall on your right) — a standing HULL, and the PARTS it is cut into, each with an id of its own. What you may say about a part: a NAME (the human's own word for it), a MATERIAL (one colour word), and a small op BY PART ID — raise it, cut a hole through its top, mirror it, or take it out. Nothing else exists here — no meshes, no vertices, no triangles, no code, no files, no libraries, no textures, lights or cameras, and no units but the ones the parts were given in. **You do not write geometry, and you do not add profiles.** The drawing already said what the shape is; you say what it is.
reply: {"parts":[{"id":"part:1","name":"wall","material":"stone","why":"the low run along the east edge"},{"id":"part:2","name":"turret","material":"green","why":"the tall one at the corner"},{"id":"part:9","name":"ghost","why":"a part this hull does not have"}],"steps":[{"id":"s1","op":"boss","part":"part:2","height":0.6,"why":"a turret stands over its wall"},{"id":"s2","op":"extrude","part":"part:1","profile":"stroke:1","depth":2,"why":"outside the part vocabulary"}]}

dropped: the colour word “stone” on part:1 is not one the shard can paint
a part entry is about part:9, and this hull has no such part — its parts are part:1, part:2
a step about part:1 whose op is “extrude” — outside the part vocabulary (boss, cut, mirror, remove)

why: The reply the e2e drives the loop with, and it is deliberately imperfect: a colour word outside the closed list, one part id this hull does not have, and one op outside the part vocabulary. Every one of them is dropped and counted, and what could be used still lands — part:1 keeps the name it was given and loses only the colour, which is *what it cannot use, it leaves* seen three times in one reply. The two steps are the boss and the engine’s own clip to the hull.
